extracted.intended_audience: OSTP Director, federal policymakers, AI policy makers, civil society organizations, and AI governance stakeholders
extracted.subtask_short: AI Bill of Rights policy statement
extracted.subtask_description: A civil-society policy statement endorsing and specifying expectations for the U.S. Office of Science and Technology Policy's 'AI Bill of Rights', listing rights, implementation strategies, and normative standards the Bill should include and build upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set out concrete principles, avoid qualifiers, build on prior initiatives, be bipartisan
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI Bill of Rights should 'set out concrete principles, avoid qualifiers, build on prior AI initiatives, and be bipartisan.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAIDP urges the Bill to be concrete and meaningful, to build on established frameworks (e.g., OECD AI Principles, Universal Guidelines for AI), and to pursue bipartisan consensus so it leads to concrete outcomes rather than vague aspirational language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to know when and how AI influences decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Your right to know when and how AI is influencing a decision that affects your civil rights and civil liberties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bill should require notice/transparent disclosure when automated systems affect individuals' opportunities in housing, employment, credit, education, etc., so affected people can understand AI's role in decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from un-audited, biased, or insufficiently representative AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Your freedom from being subjected to AI that hasn’t been carefully audited to ensure that it’s accurate, unbiased, and has been trained on sufficiently representative data sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires comprehensive auditing, use of appropriate datasets, and processes to verify accuracy and non-discrimination; implies standards for dataset representativeness, auditing frequency, and remediation when problems are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from pervasive or discriminatory surveillance
rubrics_metrics.description: Your freedom from pervasive or discriminatory surveillance and monitoring in your home, community, and workplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bill should guard against AI-enabled surveillance practices that are discriminatory or pervasive. CAIDP and UGAI also advocate prohibitions on secret profiling and systems akin to social credit scores that enable government surveillance and discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to meaningful recourse for algorithmic harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Your right to meaningful recourse if the use of an algorithm harms you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The framework should provide mechanisms for redress, explanation, appeal, and remediation when algorithms cause tangible harms to individuals, including access to remedies and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use federal procurement to enforce rights (refuse to buy noncompliant tech)
rubrics_metrics.description: The federal government could refuse to buy software or technology products that fail to respect these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procurement is a leverage point: the Bill should enable or direct federal buyers to exclude technologies that do not meet the Bill’s standards, creating market incentives for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require federal contractors to use compliant technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal contractors could be required to use technologies that adhere to this 'bill of rights.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply contract requirements and clauses to ensure technologies procured or used by contractors meet specified fairness, transparency, security, and accountability standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt new laws and regulations where needed
rubrics_metrics.description: New laws and regulations could be adopted to implement the Bill of Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal and regulatory action is an explicit implementation strategy; the Bill should identify gaps where statutory or regulatory authority is needed and recommend legislative/regulatory remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe and Effective Systems (OSTP Blueprint principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Safe and Effective Systems (one of the OSTP 'Five Principles' / 'Fair AI Practices').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems should be designed, tested, and monitored to ensure safety and effectiveness for intended use; the Blueprint frames this as a foundational principle allocating rights and responsibilities in development and deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic Discrimination Protections / Fairness and Equity (OSTP Blueprint principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithmic Discrimination Protections (Fairness and Equity) (one of the OSTP 'Five Principles').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bill should include explicit protections against algorithmic discrimination, aligning with commitments to fairness, inclusive growth, and countering bias (references to OECD and other commitments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Privacy (OSTP Blueprint principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Privacy (one of the OSTP 'Five Principles').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect individuals’ data and limit uses that infringe privacy; the Bill should incorporate privacy safeguards appropriate to automated systems and data-driven decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Explanation / Transparency (OSTP Blueprint principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and Explanation (Transparency) (one of the OSTP 'Five Principles').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require meaningful notice and explanations about AI-driven decisions; transparency obligations should enable understanding of how AI affects rights and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Alternatives, Consideration, and Fallback / Accountability (OSTP Blueprint principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Alternatives, Consideration, and Fallback (Accountability) (one of the OSTP 'Five Principles').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure human oversight, options for human decision-making or fallback, and accountability mechanisms for automated decisions that affect individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal Guidelines for AI (UGAI) principles and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: UGAI principles: fairness, accountability, transparency, and human determination; obligations for accuracy, security, and public safety; prohibitions (e.g., secret profiling, social credit scores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAIDP recommends the Bill build on UGAI: include basic rights and obligations, accuracy/security/public safety standards, and explicit prohibitions on harmful practices such as secret profiling and social-credit-like systems that enable surveillance and discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance democratic values and broad social inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: AI policies should advance democratic values and promote broad social inclusion based on fundamental rights, democratic institutions, and the rule of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bill should be grounded in human rights and democratic norms rather than purely technical or industry-centered goals; policy design and implementation should center inclusion and rule-of-law protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive auditing and diverse perspectives in system development
rubrics_metrics.description: AI developers should use appropriate data sets and audit systems comprehensively, and have diverse perspectives around the table to anticipate and fix problems before products are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation includes technical audits, dataset governance, and institutional practices (diverse teams, participatory design) to detect and prevent harms prior to deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely finalization and concrete outcomes to avoid harms and preserve leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI Bill of Rights must be finalized and implemented without undue delay; delays impose real costs on individuals and US leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAIDP emphasizes timeliness: failure to produce clear principles and action means continued opaque automated decision-making harming opportunities and undermining U.S. policy leadership; the Bill should lead to actionable next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align with established international frameworks (OECD, DOD, G7, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bill should build on established AI policy frameworks such as the OECD AI Principles, Universal Guidelines for AI, Department of Defense ethical AI principles, and international commitments (G7) to transparency and fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage existing international norms and commitments to ensure coherence, interoperability, and legitimacy; use these frameworks as models for rights, responsibilities, and implementation mechanisms.
